responses.sql: SELECT t.ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS matched_records FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON t.transreg = a.translink WHERE a.patsim > 0.439 GROUP BY t.ordertypedist

assumptions.assumption: The count is of matched (advanced behaviour, transaction record) pairs. Since transreg is the primary key and translink is a single value, each qualifying behaviour record matches at most one transaction, so this equals the number of distinct transaction records.
A NULL ordertypedist is kept as its own group. GROUP BY puts NULLs in a single group, so no special handling is needed.

responses.sql: SELECT t.ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS matched_records FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON t.transreg = a.translink WHERE a.patsim > 0.439 GROUP BY t.ordertypedist

assumptions.assumption: The count is of matched (advancedbehavior, transactionrecord) pairs. Since transreg is the primary key and translink is a single value, each behaviour record matches at most one transaction, so this equals the number of behaviour records.
A NULL ordertypedist forms its own group, which GROUP BY does by default. It is returned as NULL.

responses.sql: SELECT t.ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS matched_records FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON t.transreg = a.translink WHERE a.patsim > 0.439 GROUP BY t.ordertypedist;

assumptions.assumption: The number of matched records is counted as the number of advanced behaviour/transaction record pairs (join rows). Since translink is a single foreign key per advanced behaviour record and transreg is a primary key, each advanced behaviour record matches at most one transaction record, so this equals the number of matched advanced behaviour records.
Rows with NULL ordertypedist form their own group; GROUP BY places NULLs in one group, and the column is returned as NULL for that group.
